executiveSummary: GM0164's 2025 identity, boundary, population, neighbourhood, place, settlement and safety-region inputs reconcile, and the deterministic gate covers all ten canonical presets, six checkpoints and eight services. Release remains correction-required. The named Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset gives higher-sandy Hengelo a sustained internal flood field of 0.466420, 6,466 affected people-equivalent by T+72 and essentially frozen T+24-T+72 service state without a selected major-river source, water level, defence state or connected LIWO footprint. Official evidence instead distinguishes Twentekanaal, Berflobeek/Bornsebeek and urban-drainage operations, and characterizes regional flood risk as limited while drought increases. Eight materially nonzero hazards reuse exactly the same complete 62-neighbourhood order. A controlled woodland source in Stadspark Weusthag Noord yields direct fire 0.659460 and smoke 0.632381, yet the source neighbourhood ranks 44th. Eight boundary-road links, three stations and schedules are useful skeletons but do not establish A1/A35, local crossing, acute-care, industrial, responder or supply access; ZGT confirms that specialist emergency care is in Almelo, not at Hengelo. Public water assets and observations, grid planning, antennas, schools and emergency guidance do not establish live topology, capacity, occupancy, backup, support points or recovery. Retain official public context and arithmetic, but suppress exact local hazard, access, outage and recovery claims unless publisher, version, valid time, coverage, licence, evidence class and Unknown/NoData are explicit.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: GM0164 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place and settlement geography and statistics
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; CBS/PDOK inputs retrieved 31 August 2026; BRT TOP10NL source date 1 July 2025
supports: The annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK input identifies GM0164 as Hengelo (O.) and reports 83,655 residents, density 1,375/km², 21.2% aged 65 or older and 16,485 one-person households; the generated centre is inside the 2025 boundary.

Sixty-two published neighbourhood rows sum to 83,665 residents, ten above the municipality total (+0.012%); households sum to 39,960 and rounded age-65-plus rows to 17,715. Deterministic allocation reconciles to 83,655 without rewriting observations.

One active BAG woonplaats is Hengelo. BRT supplies five settlement labels: Hengelo and Beckum as woonkernen and Driene, Oele and Twekkelo as buurtschappen. The labels carry no independent resident or emergency-capacity measure.

CBS neighbourhoods and registered residents are annual administrative context, not brook catchments, woodland/fuel cells, utility zones or event-time people. BAG/PDOK place data carries Public Domain Mark 1.0; null, suppressed and not-applicable values remain NoData.

evidenceSources.title: Klimaatadaptatiestrategie, Programma Water en Riolering 2023-2027 and 2026 water programme
evidenceSources.edition: Climate-adaptation strategy adopted 9 March 2022; water/sewer programme 2023-2027; 2026-2029 budget inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The municipality's Twente/Hengelo climate atlas screens possible 2050 water nuisance, flood, drought and heat effects down to parcel scale. It is planning evidence with assumptions, not an event-valid observation, forecast or universally licensed operational raster.

The water/sewer programme describes disconnecting rainwater, storage/wadis and more room for water along Elsbeek, Berflobeek and Drienerbeek. The 2026 budget says two Berflobeek sections and multiple pump renovations are being undertaken, a blue-veins capacity map is still to be produced, and 105 groundwater wells are planned for real-time monitoring.

The public asset inventory reports 637,214 m gravity sewer, 95,348 m mechanical sewer, 91 sewer pumps, 290 pressure installations and 229,248 m drainage. Inventory/planning totals do not reveal incident-time hydraulic topology, compatible capacity, blockages, power/backup, maintenance or recovery.

The municipality records increasing coordination with Vitens due to drinking-water scarcity. This supports a drought/supply dependency class, not a current shortage, pressure/quality state or service outage.

evidenceSources.title: Hengelo brook and treatment context, IMWA/DAMO assets and Waterinfo observations
evidenceSources.edition: Vechtstromen decisions 2022 and 2024; HWH snapshot 3 September 2026; Waterinfo snapshot retrieved 2 September 2026 at 18:03 UTC
supports: Vechtstromen documents Berflobeek/Bornsebeek maintenance near the A1 and Plein Westermaat to retain discharge capacity and reduce water-nuisance probability, plus RWZI Hengelo process decisions. These are location/date-specific works, not universal completed protection.

The partial national CC BY-SA 4.0 HWH aggregation assigns 293 points to GM0164 by full 2025 boundary containment: 285 weirs, five surface-water pumps, two sewer pumps and RWZI Hengelo. Contributor completeness varies; records do not establish connectivity, compatible capacity units, current control, telemetry, power/backup or repair.

The CC0 Waterinfo snapshot assigns three NAP point observations at Hengelo Koppelleiding and the Hengelo lock above/below, observed 2 September 2026 at 17:30 UTC and 33 minutes old at retrieval. Two carried a normal-water-level class and one no class.

Rijkswaterstaat says public Waterinfo is not mission-critical and does not cover every water body. A point observation/class is not a Twentekanaal or brook surface, threshold elsewhere, breach, inundation scenario, operating instruction or T+72 forecast.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Risicoprofiel Twente 2025, care-risk profile and LIWO flood-scenario catalogue
evidenceSources.edition: Regional risk profile adopted 23 April 2026 and officially published 2 June 2026; LIWO deployment 2025.1.6; inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The current profile describes higher sandy ground with brooks and canals, limited overall flood risk, increasing drought/nature-fire risk, salt-extraction and subsurface-storage hazards, international A1/A35/rail and pipeline dangerous-goods corridors, vital 380 kV/drinking-water/RWZI functions and cross-border Germany dependencies.

GHOR's 2025 care-risk profile identifies cyberattack, energy outage, fire in a care institution with less self-reliant occupants, terrorism/crime, infectious disease and drinking-water contamination as material care disruptions. Regional relevance is not a Hengelo event or local magnitude.

LIWO is an irregularly released expert scenario catalogue, not a live warning or forecast. No expert-selected Rhine/Meuse/IJssel, Twentekanaal, brook, regional-defence or pluvial footprint is bound to the audited run.

A causal flood adapter must preserve scenario/release, source water, boundary hydrograph and datum, defence/breach/overtopping/control state, connected footprint, depth/velocity/arrival/duration/recession, probability, CRS/resolution/units, coverage, NoData, uncertainty and approval. Verify layer-specific LIWO reuse terms before packaging.

evidenceSources.title: Omgevingsvisie Stedelijk Hengelo and TOP10NL Weusthag woodland eligibility
evidenceSources.edition: Municipal environmental vision dated 16 October 2025; inspected TOP10NL woodland feature registered 25 August 2011 with source actuality 1 January 2010
supports: The municipality describes Weusthag as about 200 hectares of green rural area with woods, hedgerows, water and recreation; the A1 divides it, the northern part emphasizes nature, and its waters provide rain storage.

At the controlled source near [6.798433,52.288996], TOP10NL feature 033e691d-77d3-5af5-b1c0-1f3fa855aa38 classifies deciduous woodland from 2010 aerial source material, registered in 2011 at reported accuracy 0.1. TOP10NL is generally CC BY 4.0.
Policy and old/static land cover support woodland/drought eligibility only, not current fuel, moisture, ignition, perimeter, smoke, access, firefighting water, recreation occupancy or suppression.

evidenceSources.title: Twentekanaal HCH, industrial-water dependency and external-safety policy
evidenceSources.edition: Current HCH page, December 2025 measure study and January 2025 external-safety evaluation inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The municipality says HCH concentrations returned to pre-2024-peak levels after flushing but the Twentekanaal still did not meet Water Framework Directive requirements. A relative decline or normal water level is not a safe/zero contamination state.

The 2025 study reports Nobian draws about 1,700 m³/hour of canal water for salt-production/cooling processes connected with Warmtenet Hengelo, and considers uncertain treatment options. This is a material industrial water/heat dependency, not live flow, operability or guaranteed treatment performance.

The January 2025 policy identifies A1, A35, rail and pipelines as dangerous-goods routes, relatively high risk ceilings on Hengelo-Oldenzaal and the Twentekanaallijn, and a permitted transition ending dangerous-goods shunting at the emplacement. Permit/planning state must not be recast as a verified completed operational change.

Facility/corridor presence never implies a release. A natural-hazard cascade requires current competent-authority/operator evidence for substance class, containment, plume/water pathway, protective action, shutdown/restart and valid time.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat / ProRail / OVapi / NDW / Provincie Overijssel
evidenceSources.title: NWB boundary-road skeleton, rail stations, transit and current-road context
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 1 August 2026; ProRail station register and GTFS version 9543; public snapshots retrieved 2-3 September 2026
supports: Monthly CC0 NWB produces eight logical boundary links: A35 to Enschede and Borne, A1 to Dinkelland, Borne and Enschede, N739 to Haaksbergen, N342 to Dinkelland and N346 to Hof van Twente, with nominal scenario-unit ceilings 260 or 150. Consecutive/shared corridor edges are not additive capacity.

ProRail's manually updated CC0 register identifies Hengelo, Hengelo Oost and Hengelo Gezondheidspark; GTFS version 9543 contains 137 stop areas. Static geometry/schedules do not establish passengers, service, accessibility, evacuation throughput or restoration.

The transport skeleton does not establish event-time continuity over Twentekanaal/brooks/rail, internal access to industry/RWZI, acute transfer to Almelo, A1/A35 corridor performance or cross-border freight/responders. Zero covered NDW current situations is no usable record at publication time, not proof of open roads.

evidenceSources.publisher: Ziekenhuisgroep Twente / Gemeente Hengelo / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO
evidenceSources.title: Acute-care, electricity-planning, communications, education and first-72-hour public context
evidenceSources.edition: Current ZGT and municipality pages inspected 3 September 2026; public deployment snapshots retrieved 31 August-3 September 2026
supports: ZGT explicitly says Hengelo has no emergency department: its out-of-hours GP post refers patients needing specialist emergency care to the ED in Almelo. ZGT describes Hengelo chiefly as diagnostics, outpatient, day-treatment and short-stay; some radiodiagnostics are time-limited. Zero RIVM acute-care questionnaire points inside GM0164 is coverage, not no hospital or no care demand.

One postcode sample identifies Enexis area HGLW Hengelo Weideweg with quarterly/monthly capacity and queue planning values. The product is described as open data but an exact licence identifier was not found; one sample is not municipal topology, live load, outage, switching, reserve or restoration.

Public snapshots assign 183 RDI antenna records and 69 DUO education-use locations. RDI licence/cadence is unstated; DUO is daily CC BY with version unspecified. Points do not establish coverage/backhaul/power, people present, reception designation, supplies, accessibility or operation.

Hengelo instructs residents to use NL-Alert, RTV Oost 89.4 FM and prepare for the first 72 hours, while stating that municipality and safety region are still investigating where/how emergency support points will be established. Guidance/exercises are not live household preparedness, activated support sites, stocks, crews or completed actions.

residualLimitations: This is a deterministic first-72-hour planning stress test, not a KNMI, WMCN/LIWO, Vechtstromen, RWS, VRT, municipality, ZGT or operator warning, forecast, probability, evacuation order, casualty model or restoration commitment.
No expert-selected Hengelo Rhine/Meuse/IJssel, Twentekanaal, lock, Berflobeek/Bornsebeek/Elsbeek/Drienerbeek, groundwater, sewer or pluvial scenario with connected footprint drives the simulation.

The current river field is an internal diagnostic, not verified metres; source, hydrograph/datum, defence/control, arrival, velocity, duration/recession, resolution, units, coverage, NoData, uncertainty and layer licence are absent.

The municipal climate atlas is 2050 planning screening down to parcel scale, not an event-valid reusable depth raster, live passability layer or current sewer model; unavailable cells/technical metadata remain Unknown.

Completed, planned, in-progress and investigated water works are location/date-specific. Pump renovations, blue-vein mapping, groundwater sensors and Berflobeek work cannot be generalized or presumed complete/current without commissioning evidence.
CBS generalized polygons and labels do not resolve terrain, brook/canal compartments, sewers, buildings, paving, shade, woodland, facilities, corridors or household exposure.
CBS values are rounded/suppressed; district heating and charging are absent everywhere and other fields are partly missing. Null is Unknown, never zero service, demand or safety.

Registered residents omit ZGT patients/staff, industrial workers, pupils, station passengers, commuters, responders and Weusthag/event visitors; no authorized event-time transient ledger is available.

TOP10NL Weusthag land cover is old/static eligibility only; the focused ignition is synthetic and no live fuel, moisture, perimeter, wind, access, firewater, recreation occupancy or suppression state is available.

Static NWB, ProRail and GTFS geometry/schedules do not establish live roads, canal/brook/rail crossings, rail/bus service, evacuation, emergency priority or freight state/capacity; consecutive corridor edges are non-additive.
Zero covered NDW situations is no usable report at publication time, not proof roads or crossings are open. Local water-driven failures can fall outside that snapshot.

HWH points and inventory/project pages do not establish full water/wastewater topology, compatible capacity units, control logic, operation, power backup, staff or repair. Missing fields/assets remain Unknown.

Three Waterinfo records are dated local point measurements from a non-mission-critical public service; normal classification is not citywide safety, a forecast, connected inundation or operating instruction.

No complete public physical Enexis feeder/switching, Vitens pipe/pressure/quality, gas district/valve, telecom backhaul, Warmtenet or municipal sewer topology is authorized in the model; one postcode sample is planning context only.

ZGT Hengelo is not an ED; its services and RIVM zero assignment do not establish incident-time care acceptance, staffing, occupancy, medicines, oxygen, generator/fuel endurance, water/sanitation, transfer capacity or restoration.

RDI and DUO points identify registered installation/use, not communications coverage, activated reception, people present, capacity, supplies, power backup or recovery; RDI reuse terms are unresolved.

Industrial and hazardous-transport source classes do not imply a release. HCH pre-peak levels are not zero/safe, and no current substance, containment, plume, firefighting-water, shutdown or restart state drives the model.
Cyber disruption has no named target, architecture, attack/detection/containment state or authoritative operational evidence; generic service loss is not an observed incident.

The municipality's 72-hour guidance and resilience exercises do not measure household preparedness or identify activated support points. No validated inventory exists for reception, pumps/generators, fuel, food/water/medicine stocks, crews, vehicles, mutual aid or completed actions.

Event-attributable essential-service person-hours is a matched-no-event weighted availability proxy, not customer outage-hours, injuries, mortality, evacuation, displacement or welfare loss; 72 hours excludes prolonged contamination and reconstruction.
